title: Private pool sampling override cascade causing customer eval drift
creator: Lena Park
description:
Summary: A mid-market customer running a Private deployment reported reproducible eval regressions after our recent sampling-defaults change. Their golden prompts began producing extra trailing tokens and occasionally truncated JSON outputs. This ticket tracks investigation, customer communication, hotfix rollout, and longer-term preventative work.

Observed behavior: After the sampling-defaults migration, several customer evals that previously terminated on a provided stop sequence now either include extra filler text after the stop (overgeneration) or cut off earlier than expected (truncation). The issue is isolated to Private pools with route-level sampling overrides and occurs intermittently across model variants.

Hypothesis: A change to the sampling inheritance logic allowed an empty sampling override to cascade from route -> pool -> runtime, where "null"/empty sentinel values were interpreted by the runtime as an explicit switch to deterministic/"greedy" decode path. That path short-circuits the stop-sequence precedence logic under specific code paths, causing both overgeneration and premature termination depending on timing of KV-cache flushes and prefix merging.

Customer notes: Customer provided two failing eval examples, internal eval harness reproducer, and a Private deployment manifest (sanitized). They reported increased error rate in their nightly regression suite starting the day the defaults rolled out.
investigation_steps: 03/02 reproduce locally with customer prompt + private pool config using their manifest; initially couldn't reproduce on hosted runtime
03/02 add debug logging to routing layer to capture sampling override payloads sent to host agents
03/03 observed that route config for the customer included an empty 'sampling' object after migration; routing serialized it as '{}', runtime interpreted '{}' differently than missing field
03/03 instrumented runtime to log decode-path selection and stop-seq evaluation order; found cases where 'greedy' path bypassed stop-seq matcher when prefix length > 512
03/04 correlated with KV-cache eviction logs; race where prefix merging + greedy optimization caused off-by-one token emission
03/04 validated behavior against two model families (gpt-ish open model and L2 family) to rule out model-specific tokenization issues
03/05 tested an explicit stop_seq override in route config -> suppressed regression, confirming inheritance bug
03/06 created minimized unit test in runtime repo reproducing precedence bug deterministically
comments: Lena Park (creator) 2025-02-12: Filed after customer call. Customer impact: nightly pipelines failing validations ~8% failure delta. Escalated to P0 due to production impact.
Marco Ruiz (assignee) 2025-02-13: Started triage. Prioritized reproducer, asked infra for private pool access token and logs. Linking customer artifacts (Drive link) and internal reproducer PR.
Amelia Chen (PM) 2025-02-14: Noted this aligns with recent sampling defaults rollout. Please include rollback plan and expected customer-facing message templates.
SRE on-call 2025-02-15: Confirmed no capacity or kernel OOM signals correlated; logs point to config handling rather than resource pressure.
Marco Ruiz 2025-02-16: Hotfix branch created that treats empty sampling objects as 'no-override' sentinel and preserves stop-seq precedence. Running integration tests against private pool replica.
QA 2025-02-17: Added regression tests to ensure stop_seq is honored for deterministic and stochastic decode paths across prefix sizes up to 4096 tokens.
Customer success 2025-02-18: Drafted customer message — hotfix will be deployed to their private control plane during a 2-hour window; offered rollback if issues persist.
attachments: GitHub PR: runtime#1489 hotfix - sampling inheritance sentinel handling https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1489
resolution_summary: (in progress) Deployed hotfix to customer's Private control plane that treats empty/{} sampling objects as 'inherit from parent' rather than an explicit override. Initial rollout reduced customer's nightly regression failures from ~8% delta to <0.5% in canary. Additional fixes added to runtime unit tests and integration harness to prevent decode-path bypass of stop_seq matcher. Full rollout scheduled after downstream validation.
follow_up_actions: Add schema-level validation in Control Plane to reject empty sampling objects or convert them to explicit 'inherit' sentinel before persisting
Add end-to-end tests covering stop_seq precedence across greedy/stochastic code paths and across prefix lengths up to 8k tokens
Audit recent sampling-defaults migration for other config types that may have empty object fallthrough semantics
Postmortem with timeline and customer impact summary; craft postmortem public notes for CSM if requested
Consider adding a feature flag to opt-in to new sampling inheritance semantics with telemetry gating
